title: Cup product on module cohomology via acyclic resolutions
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], F,G O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and p,q nonnegative integers. Write H^n(X,-) for the right-derived global-sections cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] and F\otimes G for the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. A computing resolution of F is a nonnegative complex K with a quasi-isomorphism F[0]\to K, an injective resolution F\to I [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and a comparison K\to I extending the augmentation, whose global-sections map induces isomorphisms in every degree. A resolution pairing consists of computing resolutions of F,G,F\otimes G and restriction-compatible O_X-linear bilinear maps K_F^r(V)\times K_G^s(V)\to K_{F\otimes G}^{r+s}(V), obeying the signed total-tensor Leibniz rule [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and extending s\otimes t in degree zero. The usual sheaf cup product H^p(X,F)\times H^q(X,G)\to H^{p+q}(X,F\otimes G) is characterized as the unique Gamma(X,O_X)-bilinear map that, for every such resolution pairing, carries the cohomology classes of two global cocycles to the class of their paired cocycle. The classes are transported via the comparison to I and the canonical injective-resolution identification, not an arbitrary isomorphism. Equivalently, this is the map induced by RGamma(F)\otimes^L RGamma(G)\to RGamma(F\otimes^L G)\to RGamma(F\otimes G); Godement resolutions compute the characterization.

proof.text: Use the computing resolution and pairing definitions now factored into the data module; their identities and fields are unchanged.

The homology projection is epi, and cycles conversion, comparison homology and injective-resolution identification are isomorphisms. ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective therefore gives surjectivity of every computing resolution class map. Signed Leibniz applied to the two cocycles gives a target cocycle with the prescribed paired section; its subtype value determines it uniquely.

Take one computing tensor pairing. Its sectionwise bilinear map restricts to cycles, and composing with the target class map is bilinear. Apply resolution invariance with D = E to show this map is constant on both fibres of the surjective input class maps. The proved bilinear_desc_surjective lemma constructs and verifies the descended bilinear map.

For an arbitrary second pairing E, lift its two input classes to cocycles for D and form their paired cycle. Resolution invariance identifies its output class with the prescribed output for E. This gives IsModuleCupProduct for the descended map.

To compare two maps satisfying the characterization, lift arbitrary input cohomology classes to cycles in D and form their paired cycle. Both maps take the same value, namely its output class. LinearMap extensionality in both variables proves uniqueness.

proof_origin.place: Acyclic-resolution characterization; proved surjectivity, cycle product, bilinear descent and uniqueness, with computing-pairing existence and cross-resolution invariance split off
